residencyRequirements.description: Either spouse must have been ordinarily resident in Nova Scotia for at least one year immediately before the divorce application (Divorce Act, RSC 1985, c. 3, s.3(1)).

waitingPeriod.description: No mandatory waiting period after filing. The one-year separation must be complete before or at the time the divorce order is granted.

noFault.name: One-Year Separation
noFault.description: Spouses have lived separate and apart for at least one year immediately preceding the determination of the divorce application.

fault.name: Physical or Mental Cruelty
fault.description: The respondent has treated the petitioner with physical or mental cruelty of such a kind as to render intolerable the continued cohabitation of the spouses.

terminology.alimony: Support (Nova Scotia term under the Parenting and Support Act, RSNS 1989, c. 160 — formerly the Maintenance and Custody Act, renamed in 2017); also referred to as 'spousal support' when invoking the federal Divorce Act
terminology.maritalProperty: Matrimonial Property (Matrimonial Property Act, RSNS 1989, c. 275)

legalCitations.description: Federal divorce statute — governs divorce proceedings in all provinces and territories
Nova Scotia statute — equal division of matrimonial assets on marriage breakdown (s.12 — equal sharing presumption)

legalCitations.code: Parenting and Support Act, RSNS 1989, c. 160
legalCitations.description: Nova Scotia statute — parenting arrangements, parenting time, contact, and support obligations (formerly the Maintenance and Custody Act, renamed in 2017)
Federal guidelines for calculating child support amounts
Procedural rules for Supreme Court of Nova Scotia proceedings

basic.name: Petition for Divorce
basic.description: Initiates the divorce proceeding in the Supreme Court of Nova Scotia (Family Division)

basic.name: Divorce Order
basic.description: Draft order to be submitted to court for signature

childSupportGuidelines.notes: Federal Child Support Guidelines apply in all provinces.

spousalSupportGuidelines.notes: SSAG are advisory only — not legislatively mandated but widely applied by Nova Scotia courts. Nova Scotia uses the term 'support' (Parenting and Support Act, RSNS 1989, c. 160) in provincial proceedings.

effectiveDateRule: 31 days after the divorce order is made, unless the court varies the effective date or both parties waive the waiting period (Divorce Act, s.12).
certificateNote: A Certificate of Divorce may be obtained from the court office after the effective date of the Divorce Order (Divorce Act, s.12(7)).

filingFees.notes: Fee waiver may be available for parties who qualify. Contact the Supreme Court of Nova Scotia for current fees.
